subject: Finexus VPC patch runway and ops authorization
messages:
From: Sara Lambert <sara.lambert@finexus.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@finexus.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Planned kernel/security patching - VPC/private footprint

Hi Sean,

We're planning a quarterly maintenance window for our private Redwood deployment in our AWS VPC (finexus-prod-us-west-2). Security team flagged CVE-2026-3145 in the k8s node images and wants a coordinated patch. Before we schedule anything, we need: 

- A simple change window estimate (duration per tranche and per AZ).
- Confirmation of the recommended rollback path if a node fails post-patch.
- Any pinning guidance: we currently have runtime pinned to rwd-1.3.2; do you recommend a short-lived staging pin?

Target week: June 21-25 (narrow window). We prefer evenings PST to minimize business impact. Can Redwood provide an ops lead and an emergency contact? Also attaching our initial patch matrix.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Lambert
Head of Platform Engineering, Finexus
Attachment: finexus_patch_matrix_v1.xlsx

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lambert <sara.lambert@finexus.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Planned kernel/security patching - VPC/private footprint

Sara — thanks for the heads up and the matrix. High-level answers below; I'll follow with an ops playbook draft and a proposed canary schedule by EOD tomorrow.

Quick summary:
- Window estimate: 60–90 minutes per AZ tranche (includes drain, patch, restart, smoke tests). If you stagger AZs with a 30–45 minute delay between tranches we expect total wall-clock ~3–4h.
- Rollback path: primary approach is instant re-pin and rollback to runtime rwd-1.3.2 + node reimage if needed. We'll maintain a warm spare pool during the window to accelerate recovery.
- Pinning guidance: recommend an adaptive pin: create a short-lived "maintenance-pin" tag for the target hosts during the patch. Hold control-plane at rwd-1.3.2 for one canary tranche, then unpin progressively after successful validation.

Ops lead and contacts:
- Sean Gallagher, Senior Customer Reliability Manager — +1 (415) 555-0123, pager: +1 (877) 555-0199
- Neha Kapoor, Private Deployments Lead — neha_kapoor@redwood.com (ops lead for rollback)

Attachments: I'll attach our rollback playbook and a sample canary schedule.

Action items for Finexus: confirm preferred start date/time (we can do evenings PST on any day in your target week), and whether you want us to own the canary tranche or hand the first tranche to your team.

—Sean

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Planned kernel/security patching - VPC/private footprint

Looping in some technical detail for the patch playbook. Karthik, please flag anything I'm missing.

Playbook highlights (draft):
1) Pre-window (48–72h):
   - Snapshot control-plane config and export KV cache.
   - Reserve warm spares (2 nodes per AZ) and validate image signatures.
   - Run smoke tests on staging with same image bundle.

2) Canary tranche (AZ-a):
   - Place canary nodes into maintenance pin: runtime pinned to candidate rwd-1.4.0-rc1.
   - Drain pods gracefully (max grace 90s), apply OS kernel patch, reboot, validate runtime and model service health (token-level smoke).
   - Hold for 60 minutes observation window with automated SLO checks (latency <= 150ms p95).

3) Rollout tranches (AZ-b, AZ-c):
   - 30–45 minute start gap between tranches.
   - If any SLO breach or >1% error increase, trigger rollback for the tranche.

4) Rollback steps (fast path):
   - Re-pin runtime controller to rwd-1.3.2 globally and signal node managers to redeploy.
   - Evacuate suspect nodes and replace from warm spares.
   - If automated rollback fails, escalate to manual rebuild (node reimage from pre-approved AMI).

5) Post-window:
   - 24h stability watch, telemetry digest to Finexus, and a short postmortem if anomalies occur.

Notes:
- For network quiesce we recommend applying a short BGP withdrawal window only if you anticipate L7 floooding; otherwise normal cordon/drain is sufficient.
- We will maintain an audit trail (audit.log + doc link) and produce a signed evidence bundle for your security team.

I attached the rollback playbook draft. Karthik — please review the reimage timing and the warm-spare sizing.

Neha
Private Deployments Lead
Attachment: rollback_playbook_draft.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lambert <sara.lambert@finexus.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Planned kernel/security patching - VPC/private footprint

Sara — thanks for confirming earlier this morning that Finexus prefers Redwood to run the canary tranche and that the team will monitor the rollout. Two quick clarifications and one ask: 

Clarifications:
- Warm spares: we recommend 2 warm spares per AZ for a fleet of your size; this avoids capacity dip and speeds node replacement.
- Pin expiry: maintenance-pin will auto-expire after 36 hours unless extended by a manual confirmation.

Ask:
- Please confirm: (1) target start: Tue June 22, 20:00 PST; (2) approval to run canary and push candidate runtime rwd-1.4.0-rc1. Once you confirm, we'll create a short runbook and a DocuSign approval for change record and emergency rollback sign-off (link below).

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleDriveLink

—Karthik
